subject: Private maintenance: surge mitigation and shelving guidelines for Greenfield Health VPC
messages:
From: Samuel Brant <samuel.brant@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@greenfieldhealth.com
Date: 2029-03-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Upcoming private-patch: scheduling & pinning questions

Hi Jonas,

We're starting internal planning for the April maintenance wave and wanted to lock down the approach with Redwood. Our primary asks: minimal service disruption (bursty inference traffic from our nightly billing job), clear pin/shelving rules if we see regression, and a simple rollback path that doesn't require reingesting KV caches across the fleet.

Can you share a proposed narrow window, the exact pinning semantics (how you’ll hold back versions), and what your emergency shelving criteria look like? If you have a short runbook and any network diagram notes for our on-prem transit, that would help our ops planning.

Also: we prefer a weekday evening window (US-East friendly) rather than a weekend if possible.

Thanks,
Samuel
Samuel Brant
Sr. Cloud Ops, Greenfield Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Brant <samuel.brant@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming private-patch: scheduling & pinning questions

Hi Samuel —

Thanks for the heads up. Draft proposal below; attached manifest + network diagram for your review.

High-level proposal (narrow window):
- Window: Tue 2029-04-09 22:00 - 00:30 ET (2.5 hrs). We pick a weekday evening to match your request.
- Canary tranche: 5% of traffic to a canary namespace for 30 minutes; health checks (99.95% request success, latency p50/p95 targets) before widening.
- Pinning semantics: we will pin your VPC to the current stable model artifact (artifact sha) for the duration of the window and for a 48-hour post-window observation period. Pinning prevents auto-roll to new model variants or infra-level hotfixes unless explicitly approved.
- Shelving criteria: immediate shelving if (a) inference error rate delta > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 15 minutes, (b) p95 latency regression > 75ms sustained for 10 minutes, or (c) any data-path errors related to KV corruption. Shelving action will switch traffic to the last known-good pinned artifact and initiate rollback tasks.
- Rollback approach: instant config swap to pinned artifact + staged KV warmup on edge nodes. We do NOT require full reingest; our KV warmup uses prefix caching and will converge in parallel.

Network notes: see attached network-diagram-vpc.pdf. Key callouts: please ensure the transit ACLs allow ports 6000-6010 for internal heartbeats and the egress route to Redwood's update service on 443 is reachable from your maintenance VLAN.

Attachments: patch_manifest_v2.xlsx (detailed list), network-diagram-vpc.pdf

Next steps: if this window looks good, we'll schedule an internal dry run on 2029-04-05 and prepare the rollback-checklist.txt for your team. If you want an earlier or shorter window, tell us constraints and we can adjust.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-30T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: runbook fragments + automation hooks for GFH patch

Jonas / Monica —

Dropping the checklist + automation snippets I want in the runbook. I attached a flattened rollback-checklist.txt and added inline notes below. We'll include these in the shared Drive link.

Pre-window (S-2 days):
- Validate snapshot backups for KV namespaces: run `kvctl snapshot list --since 48h --namespace gf-health`
- Confirm net ACLs (6000-6010) and BGP next-hop routes; ask GH to confirm egress to update.redwood.internal
- Stage canary images on 2 out of 10 nodes; do kernel-level compatibility test (seq-len stress).

During window:
- Start canary (5%): `trafficctl route --namespace gf-health --split 95/5 --to canary`
- Automated health checks: if any check trips, run `scripts/shelve.sh --artifact <sha> --reason <code>` (refer to attached rollback-checklist.txt for codes).

Emergency shelving/rollback (fast lane):
- Step 1: run `trafficctl force-route --namespace gf-health --artifact <last-good-sha>`
- Step 2: run KV warmup `kvctl warmup --parallel 8 --prefix /billing/` (monitored)
- Step 3: if warmup fails across majority, trigger node-level evacuation and fail to standby cluster.

Post-window: 48h watch with daily digest; if any anomaly persists, initiate full revert request to platform team.

Attachments: rollback-checklist.txt

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Orchestration
From: Samuel Brant <samuel.brant@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@greenfieldhealth.com
Date: 2029-04-01T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming private-patch: scheduling & pinning questions

Jonas,

Appreciate the detailed plan — the Wednesday evening window is acceptable. Two quick clarifications before I sign off: 
1) During the 48h post-window observation where you keep our environment pinned, are any security patches (critical CVEs) still allowed to be applied automatically, or would those require a separate emergency approval?
2) Can you confirm the expected client impact during KV warmup (we have a billing job that runs at 23:30 ET and is latency sensitive).

If you can answer above and share the Drive link to the runbook, we can route internal approvals.

Thanks,
Samuel
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Brant <samuel.brant@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-04-02T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming private-patch: scheduling & pinning questions

Hi Samuel — quick answers and final confirmations.

1) Critical security patches: any high-severity CVE fixes that affect the control plane will be handled under our emergency-security pathway and may be applied during the pinned window but only after a documented emergency approval (signed by your security lead). We'll list exceptions explicitly in the runbook. Non-control-plane infra patches that don't change runtime artifacts will be deferred until the observation window ends.

2) KV warmup impact: designed to be background-forwarding and rate-limited. Expected client-facing latency impact: negligible for p50, up to +30–40ms p95 during the first 10 minutes of parallel warmup, then returning to baseline. If your billing job's SLO cannot tolerate any p95 increase, we can shift canary start earlier (start at 22:00 with billing job at 23:30 on reduced canary traffic) or run a pre-warm step 30 minutes before your job.

Drive link (runbook & artifacts): https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D-patch-runbook

If that works, please reply with a quick accept + the name/email of the approver for emergency-security exceptions. We'll schedule dry run on 2029-04-05 20:00 ET and the live window on 2029-04-09 22:00 ET as proposed.

Cheers,
Jonas
